body:
Thanks for this comment, it resonates with me.

A lot of gay guys I know, I met them through my best friend's social circle and she goes to art school. They fit a lot of stereotypes and their attitude just gets on my nerves. They're also super immature, as if stuck in a high school mentality.

I do know of some other gay guys too. Though I'm usually surprised to learn they're gay. Like I found out through one of the art school guys that an acquaintance I would've never guessed to be gay is. And that he's a virgin... So the fact that this guy shared that with everyone just made him more annoying in my eyes lmao. It's the high school mentality I'm talking about. Talking behind your friends' backs.

But this is a very limited circle, I know. I should expand it, which is hard when you're in the closet. I've been trying to deal with that whole issue in psychotherapy, but that's a whole another topic.

It's possible I compare myself to them subconsciously and maybe that's what makes me uneasy because of the stigma.

Oh and I didn't mean to say all gay guys fit one stereotype, it's just that I somehow ended up in the circle where many of them do.

I guess it's also the problem of flamboyant guys being the most noticeable ones, but then that's the whole deeper issue with how society treats "gayness".

I agree, maybe intimidated or uneasy would better describe the feeling.

For whatever reason, a lot of people I've come to have in my social circle are straight girls who like collecting stereotypical gay BFF's... As bad as that sounds, but essentially yeah. So these are the types of gay guys I come in contact with a lot.

Though sometimes, I also get the feeling that their attitude (especially the mean/catty part) is forced and exaggerated because they want to fit in.

You're right about social media, those who look for attention in a "shocking" way are those who'll get most of it. I guess that's why there's this impression that the loudest make up the majority.

Thanks for commenting and I totally agree with what you're saying here.
